brief: Deutsche Bank's daily macro wrap reports a risk-off start to September and gives the chain behind it. Renewed US strikes on Iranian targets around the Strait of Hormuz lifted Brent 4.60% to $94.65/bbl at the close and European gas to a 3-year high of €72.22/MWh. Higher energy prices fed inflation and rate expectations, and government bond yields set multi-year highs: bund 3.34%, OAT 4.20%, gilt 5.22%, 10yr Treasury 4.80%, and Japanese 10yr above 3% for the first time in 30 years. Rising nominal and real yields pushed equities lower, S&P 500 -0.71% and Stoxx 600 -0.56%, with Asia extending the decline. Fed pricing turned hawkish, 64bps of hikes by June 2027 and 69% odds of a September hike against 27% on August 17, reinforced by Governor Barr saying the Fed should hike in September if inflation is not moderating sufficiently. Softer US data, ISM 54.6, job openings 7.271m and quits 1.9%, only temporarily eased the selloff. Euro Area flash CPI at 3.3% with core at 2.4% did not stop the ECB's Simkus saying one September hike is not enough. The RBNZ hiked 25bps to 2.75% and stronger Australian GDP raised bets on an extended RBA tightening cycle.
